source_text.body:
Auto-apply to marathon lotteries when they open
An agent checks World Marathon Majors entry pages twice daily and, when a lottery opens, uses a Claude-driven browser to create accounts, read Gmail codes, submit the form and email confirmation.
·
Nov 19, 2026
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
It runs on GitHub Actions. Twice a day, Claude Haiku reads each race's entry page, and its answer counts only if the quoted sentence is really on the page. When a lottery is open, a headless browser driven by Claude Opus logs in or creates an account, reads Gmail codes, fills the form from a YAML profile, accepts the terms and submits. It then emails a screenshot.
How it went
The source gives no results from real applications. It lists Tokyo, London, Berlin, Chicago, New York City, Sydney and Cape Town. It won't solve CAPTCHAs. If it can't apply, it emails a link and reminders instead.
Worth knowing
Expect roughly $1–3 a month, with about $1–4 of Claude usage per application and a hard cap of $8. Some races' terms forbid automated entries.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
Twice a day, check the entry pages for [list of races or URLs] and tell me when a lottery or registration window opens. When one opens, start the application using my details [name, birthdate, nationality, emergency contact], and read any verification code from my Gmail if needed. Before you submit the final form or create any new account, pause and show me what you're about to send, then email me a confirmation once I approve and it's done.
Original source: https://github.com/angelinachou/marathon-agent
